text: Everything so far works the same way once you point a stage at storage you already own. This is the same Create Stage dialog, filled in with a real S3 bucket and path.
The URL has to be exact, right down to the trailing slash — miss it, and later loads fail in ways that look unrelated to the real cause.
The bucket is only half the picture. Whatever you're loading from, the target table's columns still have to line up — this one expects twelve, in a specific order.
And none of it runs without the right context. Role and warehouse are set right here — get either one wrong, and the load never even starts.
For production, skip hardcoded keys entirely. A storage integration lets Snowflake assume your IAM role directly, so no secret key ever sits in a CREATE STAGE statement.
The sequence is the same no matter which cloud you're on: authorize once with a storage integration, point a stage at the bucket, define a file format, then COPY INTO.
Next: what happens when a load doesn't go cleanly — handling errors and validating a file before you commit to it.
